fields.description:
## The defect

`infra/scripts/install-observability.sh:12` deploys ONLY the probe:

```
install -m 0755 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/observability.sh" /usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh
```

But `observability.sh` resolves its cap scripts as **siblings of its own path**:

```
 458: DOCKER_CAP_SH="${DOCKER_CAP_SH:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/docker-storage-cap.sh}"
 925: JOURNALD_CAP_SH="${JOURNALD_CAP_SH:-...}/journald-cap.sh"
 999: VARTMP_CAP_SH="${VARTMP_CAP_SH:-...}/vartmp-cap.sh"
1092: CONTAINER_CAP_SH="${CONTAINER_CAP_SH:-...}/container-cap.sh"
```

So the deployed probe at `/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh` looks for all four cap scripts
in `/usr/local/bin/`, where the installer never put any of them. **It is four scripts, not two**
— the ticket was opened against the first two and the other two were found still broken on
2026-09-06 (see the comment folding in `exorable-gemstone-bluefish`, `1e63-bee1-5ce6-4d8f`).

## Consequences, both observed on the live host

**1. Gated percent metrics silently never publish.** `docker_storage_used_percent`,
`docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent`, `journal_used_percent`, `var_tmp_used_percent` and
`container_writable_used_percent` are each gated on a budget read from `--print-env`. With the
cap script unreachable the read fails, so the metric publishes NOTHING. That is the correct
silence-not-zero behaviour firing for an incorrect reason — the caps were installed and readable
ON DISK, just not from where the probe looked.

**2. Ungated heartbeats are pinned at a FALSE 0 — this is the serious half.** Unlike the percent
metrics they publish UNGATED, so an unreachable cap script yields 0 rather than silence.
`journal_cap_in_effect`, `var_tmp_cleanup_active` and `container_reaper_active` therefore assert
"not in force" **forever, with the mechanism genuinely in force on the host.** An alarm asserting
a false negative indefinitely is worse than a missing alarm: it trains its reader to ignore it,
and it does so while the thing it watches is actually healthy.

## How it was found

During an operator-authorised cap install on 2026-09-05. Installing both caps was NOT sufficient
to make the metrics publish; the scripts had to be placed at `/usr/local/bin/` by hand before
`docker_storage_used_percent` (63.0), `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` (100.0),
`journal_used_percent` (56.0) appeared and `journal_cap_in_effect` flipped 0 -> 1.

A second, related deployment gap surfaced in the same pass: **`journald-cap.sh` did not exist on
the host at all.** `/opt/rebar` is a deployed non-git tree predating commit `e510c64`, and nothing
had delivered the new script. It was copied over SHA-verified. That is adjacent to
`octahedral-auburn-sunfish` (5246-2ec0-1fa6-4637), which records that neither cap script appears
in any of `autodeploy.sh`'s `*_PATHS` — so a commit changing a cap signals nothing.

On 2026-09-06 the same defect was confirmed still live for `vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh`
(rc 127 on both), taking `var_tmp_used_percent` and `container_writable_used_percent` off the air
and pinning `var_tmp_cleanup_active` / `container_reaper_active` to 0 on a host where both reapers
had just been installed and were genuinely running.

## The constraint that shapes the fix

`docker-storage-cap.sh` and `journald-cap.sh` define no installed path, so their repo basename is
the only name they have and either fix direction works. **`vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh`
self-install under a DIFFERENT name** (`VAR_TMP_INSTALLED_PATH` at `vartmp-cap.sh:121`,
`CONTAINER_INSTALLED_PATH` at `container-cap.sh:124`, both `/usr/local/bin/rebar-*-cap.sh`),
because that path is the `ExecStart` of the reaper units they write. Satisfying this by the
installer direction alone would place a SECOND copy under the unprefixed name — the probe reading
one copy while the reaper timer executes the other, free to drift. For those two the resolver
direction is the one that composes.

## Why this belongs with tonight's recurring class

The probe reports a value it cannot actually measure, and the failure presents as a healthy-looking
number. Same family as: a drift gate blinded by whitespace before `plan` ever ran; a CI job casting
a passing vote without executing; a test passing vacuously because a monkeypatched TMPDIR was inert;
a cap reporting itself "in effect" after a SIGHUP that does not apply it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 - A deployed probe can reach **every** cap script it resolves at runtime — all four, not
      the first two. Either direction is acceptable per script (the installer deploys it, or
      `observability.sh` resolves it from a location the installer guarantees); the invariant is
      that no `*_CAP_SH` default names a path nothing creates. Checked by AC4's deploy-time check.
- [ ] AC2 - Defect-seeded: with a cap script absent from the deploy location, a test FAILS.
      Removing it from the installer (or from the resolver's candidate list) must turn that test
      RED. Checked by `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py
      tests/scripts/test_observability_journal.py -x`.
- [ ] AC3 - Every ungated heartbeat distinguishes "the mechanism is not in force" from "I could not
      determine whether it is in force". Publishing a confident 0 for an unreadable input is the
      defect; silence or a distinct value is the fix. This covers `journal_cap_in_effect` **and**
      `var_tmp_cleanup_active` and `container_reaper_active`, which share the shape. Coordinate
      with the probe's stated contract that a probe which cannot measure publishes NOTHING rather
      than a plausible value (`observability.sh:280`, `:487`). Note the alarms on these are
      `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` with 6/6, so silence still pages — it just stops
      asserting a false negative.
- [ ] AC4 - A check catches a deployed probe whose resolved dependencies are missing, so this is
      detected at deploy time rather than by an operator noticing metrics are absent. Checked by
      the check failing when any one cap script is withheld from a rendered install.
- [ ] AC5 - For `vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh` the fix leaves exactly ONE copy of each
      script on the host, at the `*_INSTALLED_PATH` their own `--install` writes, and the probe
      resolves that path. A test proves the installed-name layout resolves: with only
      `rebar-vartmp-cap.sh` beside the probe and no `vartmp-cap.sh`, a run publishes
      `var_tmp_used_percent` and `var_tmp_cleanup_active=1`; equivalently for
      `container_writable_used_percent` / `container_reaper_active`.
- [ ] AC6 - The `*_CAP_SH` environment overrides still take precedence over every candidate, so
      existing tests injecting a stub path are unaffected.
- [ ] AC7 - `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_var_tmp.py tests/scripts/test_observability_container_layers.py -x`
  — the two suites whose metrics are currently dead; extended with the installed-name layout case.
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py tests/scripts/test_observability_journal.py -x`
  — the two already-repaired instances, to prove the resolver change does not regress them.
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_vartmp_cap.py tests/scripts/test_container_cap.py -x` — proves the
  `*_INSTALLED_PATH` defaults the resolver couples to are unchanged.
- `make lint && make typecheck` — the commit gate.
- Post-deploy verification: after autodeploy re-materializes the probe,
  `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace rebar/host --metric-name var_tmp_used_percent`
  returns datapoints, and `var_tmp_cleanup_active` / `container_reaper_active` read 1 on a host
  where the reaper timers are in force.

## Non-goals

Not changing what the caps do. Not fixing the autodeploy `*_PATHS` gap
(`octahedral-auburn-sunfish`, which `kittenish-venomous-pittabird` was closed into). Not
restarting Docker. Not retuning any alarm: these alarms are correct, and two of them are firing on
conditions that are true.
